sections.h2: Who handles property tax in Cumberland County, NC?
sections.html:
Cumberland County Tax Administration, on the fifth floor of the Judge E. Maurice Braswell Cumberland County Courthouse at 117 Dick Street in Fayetteville, assesses real estate and collects the bills. Its main number is 910-678-7507, with its listed address as 117 Dick Street, Room 530.

The department's menu is a quick map of what a seller may need: property tax revaluation, real estate appeals, exemptions and exclusions, tax relief programs, payment plans, delinquent taxes, a surplus property list, tax foreclosure sales, and a page for the Board of Equalization and Review. Personal property, business extensions, gross receipts and motor vehicle pages sit alongside.

The county is large by North Carolina standards. The Census Bureau estimates 338,473 residents for July 2025, up from 334,728 at the 2020 census, spread over 652.56 square miles of land at about 512.9 people per square mile. Nearly a dozen town and district rates apply inside it, which the table below shows.

sections.h2: What are the Cumberland County property tax rates?
sections.html:
The countywide ad valorem rate is 49.9 cents per $100 of valuation for 2026 tax bills (fiscal year 2027), and the county page adds a 5.0-cent special recreation rate. Each town adds its own rate on top, so the total depends on where the parcel sits.

sections.h2: What flat fees show up on a Cumberland County tax bill?
sections.html:
Several service charges ride on the same bill and are quoted separately from the rate. These are the amounts the county prints:

  • Solid waste fee of $285 a year for Fayetteville residences with seven or fewer units.
  • Solid waste fee of $130 a year for unincorporated areas and all municipalities except Spring Lake.
  • Refuse tax of $342.72 a year in Hope Mills and $396.00 in Spring Lake, the latter including a $12 residential litter control fee.
  • Fayetteville residential storm water in three tiers by impervious area: $84.00 under 2,500 square feet, $168.00 from 2,501 to 4,800, and $252.00 above 4,800.
  • Residential storm water of $60 a year in Spring Lake and in Hope Mills.
  • Vehicle fees: $25 vehicle fee plus a $5 transit tax in Fayetteville, $10 in Hope Mills, and $5 each in Stedman and Spring Lake.

When you compare a sale offer against your annual carrying cost, look at the bill line by line rather than the rate alone. A move across a town line can change the charges more than the home's value would.

sections.h2: When are Cumberland County taxes due, and what if I am late?
sections.html:
Property taxes are due each September 1 and must be paid by January 5 to avoid interest, penalties or collection steps. The county's rate page gives that window in the same words for the 2026 tax bills.

State law then adds 2% interest on January 6 and three-fourths of one percent for each month or fraction after February 1 (G.S. 105-360). The county offers payment through MyCCNCPay by card, debit or electronic draft, and says to call 910-678-7507 to set up a payment arrangement.

The annual listing period for property closes January 31 under G.S. 105-307, and the county posted a reminder of that deadline on January 15, 2026.

If bills go unpaid, the county sells tax-foreclosed parcels through an outside attorney acting for the tax office. Contact that attorney's office, which the county's foreclosure page names, for sale dates and parcels in the upset bid period. State law lets the sale be set aside by redemption, paying taxes, penalties, interest and costs, before the court confirms it (G.S. 105-374).

sections.h2: How did the 2025 revaluation work in Cumberland County?
sections.html:
The county reappraised all real property effective with the 2025 tax year, after a prior revaluation dated January 1, 2017. It describes itself as on an eight-year cycle, which tracks G.S. 105-286.

  • February 21, 2025: notices mailed to owners.
  • March 24, 2025: deadline for an informal appeal to Tax Administration.
  • April 23, 2025: Board of Equalization and Review convened.
  • May 28, 2025: deadline for a formal appeal, and the board adjourned.
  • July 1, 2025: new rates using the updated values took effect, with bills mailed that August.

Those dates are history now. The pattern repeats each year in a smaller form: the board convened April 22, 2026, accepted real property appeals until its adjournment on May 20, and set hearings by letter.

sections.h2: How do I appeal a Cumberland County assessment?
sections.html:
Ask for an informal review first, then file a formal request with the Board of Equalization and Review before it adjourns. The county accepts formal requests in person at Room 543 of the courthouse, by mail to PO Box 449, Fayetteville, NC 28302, or in the secure drop box in the courthouse's rear parking lot.

Requests must be in writing. An appraiser contacts every taxpayer who appeals, and a letter gives the hearing date and time if the case proceeds to the board. The county suggests appraisals, comparable properties, income and expense statements, repair cost estimates and photos of unusual conditions as evidence.

The regular board begins no earlier than the first Monday in April and no later than the first Monday in May, and in a year without a revaluation it finishes by the third Monday after it starts unless a longer period is needed, and may not sit after July 1. A special board meets on the second Wednesday of every month except July at 3:30 p.m., and approves corrections including clerical errors. After a board decision, the owner has 30 days from the mailing date of the notice to appeal to the state Property Tax Commission (G.S. 105-290).

sections.h2: What do Census figures say about selling a house in Cumberland County?
sections.html:
The owner-occupied rate is 55.0%, so renters hold about 45% of occupied homes and rental property is a large part of the market. Median value of owner-occupied homes is $199,200 for 2020-2024, median household income is $61,291, and median gross rent is $1,222.

  • Housing units, July 2025: 146,623.
  • Households, 2020-2024: 129,758.
  • Veterans: 40,226.
  • Residents 65 and older: 15.0%.
  • Building permits issued in 2025: 1,547.
  • Mean commute to work: 21.6 minutes.

With 40,226 veterans, the disabled veteran exclusion is worth a check. It removes the first $45,000 of appraised value, with no age or income limit, on Form NCDVA-9, which a Veterans Service Officer completes first. The elderly or disabled exclusion and circuit breaker use Form AV-9 filed with the county assessor and may be accepted through June 1.

faqs.q: When are Cumberland County property taxes due?
faqs.a: They are due each September 1 and must be paid by January 5 to avoid interest. State law adds 2% interest starting January 6.

faqs.q: What is the property tax rate in the City of Fayetteville?
faqs.a: The county lists the City of Fayetteville municipal rate at 0.4495 and the county rate at 0.499, for a combined 0.9485 per $100 on 2026 bills.

faqs.q: Where do I file an appeal with the Cumberland County Board of Equalization and Review?
faqs.a: Appeals go to Tax Administration in Room 543 of the courthouse at 117 Dick Street, by mail to PO Box 449, or in the secure drop box. The request must be in writing and arrive before the board adjourns.

faqs.q: When was the last Cumberland County revaluation?
faqs.a: The county completed a revaluation for 2025, with notices mailed on February 21, 2025. The prior one was effective January 1, 2017, and state law requires reappraisal at least every eight years.

faqs.q: Who runs Cumberland County tax foreclosure sales?
faqs.a: An outside attorney conducts them on behalf of the Tax Office. Call the attorney's office listed on the county's foreclosure page for sale dates and upset bid status.
